analysis: The experiment code visibly added all three claimed pieces of the mechanism: train-only watch-time target construction from DV.watch_ratio() and duration_ms, a shared-representation scalar watch head, and a mixed censored watch loss in training. It also appears to respect the feature-leakage constraint by not using watch-time-derived values as inference inputs. However, the trusted audit found two contract-level breaks that prevent crediting the result to the hypothesis: prediction-time dataflow is unproven because predict() still delegates to SO.predict on a custom model class outside the guaranteed backend path, and the custom trainer introduced a new checkpoint/selection rule based on best training loss rather than a contract-backed visible equivalent of the parent behavior. So although the measured validation number was higher than the parent, the evidence does not establish that the approved, end-to-end mechanism actually affected served predictions under the required runtime contract.
next_lesson: When replacing a parent training stack, make prediction and checkpoint behavior explicitly contract-safe in-code before interpreting any validation gain.
